items.summary: Lupin Ltd has partnered with Sandoz to launch RanluspecTM, a biosimilar for Ranibizumab, across Europe. This launch will help to improve access to treatments for retinal and choroidal vascular diseases. The European Commission previously approved RanluspecTM in vial and syringe-filled presentations for medical use. The biosimilar targets conditions such as wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic macular edema.

Centre's EV push puts electric mobility stocks in the fast lane; M&M, Ola Electric lead rally with gains of up to 5%
items.summary: Shares of automobile and electric vehicle companies gained on Wednesday, November 11, following the Centre's decision to make electric vehicles the default choice for staff-car procurement by government ministries and departments, while doubling the Net Dealer Price (NDP) ceiling for electric cars to Rs 20 lakh. Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) and Ola Electric Mobility emerged among the top gainers in the sector, with the former leading the rally with an intra-day gain of nearly 5%.M&M climbed 4.81% to touch an intra-day high of Rs 3,449, while Ola Electric Mobility advanced 3.53% to Rs 35.16.Hyundai Motor India was another major gainer, rising 3.08% to an intra-day high of Rs 2,175, while TVS Motor Company gained 2.89% to Rs 4,636.10. Ather Energy advanced 2.40% to Rs 1,904.50.Among other automobile companies, Maruti Suzuki India rose 2.10% to Rs 13,199, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles gained 2.03% to Rs 301. JBM Auto advanced 2% to Rs 511.95, while Bajaj Auto registered the lowest gain among the nine stocks, rising 1.28% to Rs 11,120.At the last check, M&M was trading 4.5% higher, followed by TVS Motor Company, which was up 2.53%. Ola Electric Mobility gained 2.20%, while Hyundai Motor India advanced 2.3%. Maruti Suzuki India was up 2%, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Ather Energy gained 1.5% each. Bajaj Auto and JBM Auto were trading 0.5% higher each, while Ashok Leyland was flat.ALSO READ: Earnings recovery, FII revival: 5 factors that will shape Dalal Street's next move after Q2What does the Centre's new EV procurement policy say?The Department of Expenditure (DEA), under the Ministry of Finance, has revised the Net Dealer Price (NDP) ceiling for the procurement of staff cars by government ministries and departments, doubling the limit for electric vehicles to Rs 20 lakh from Rs 10 lakh for internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles.Under the revised instructions, electric vehicles have been made the default choice for government staff-car procurement. Ministries and departments are directed to ordinarily procure EVs when purchasing or replacing their existing staff cars.However, the revised instructions do not completely prohibit the purchase of conventional vehicles. Departments that consider EV procurement or deployment impractical can propose purchasing ICE vehicles, subject to justification and case-specific relaxation from the Department of Expenditure, with the required approvals.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. Gland Pharma shares jump 4% as Q2 profit jumps 58%, revenue rises 23% YoY
items.summary: Shares of Gland Pharma gained 3.89% to Rs 3,254.60 during Monday's trading session after the pharmaceutical company reported a strong performance for the September 2026 quarter, with revenue rising 23% year-on-year (YoY) and net profit surging 58%.The stock also touched a fresh 52-week high of Rs 3,345 during the session.Gland Pharma reported a 23% YoY increase in its Q2 revenue from operations to Rs 1,834 crore, from Rs 1,487 in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Net profit for the September 2026 quarter rose 58% YoY to Rs 290.8 crore, compared with Rs 183.7 crore in the same quarter last year.The company's adjusted EBITDA increased 50% year-on-year, while the adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 27%. Its profit after tax (PAT) margin also expanded by approximately 350 basis points during the quarter.Business segment performanceGland Pharma's CDMO business contributed 45% to overall revenue and recorded 31% year-on-year growth in Q2 FY27. Meanwhile, its Critical Injectables business accounted for the remaining 55% of revenue, registering growth of 18% during the quarter.The company continued to invest in research and development, with total R&D expenditure reaching Rs 107.7 crore in Q2 FY27, equivalent to 6% of consolidated revenue. This was higher than Rs 81.7 crore reported in the year-ago quarter. The expenditure was primarily directed towards complex product development and increasing the number of regulatory filings.During the September quarter, Gland Pharma launched four molecules in the US market: Sugammadex, Erythromycin, Fluorouracil and Atropine Sulfate.The company also filed 11 Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs) and received 10 approvals during Q2 FY27. With these additions, its cumulative US ANDA filings reached 399, of which 350 had been approved and 49 were awaiting approval.Management commentaryCommenting on the quarterly performance, Srinivas Sadu, Executive Chairman of Gland Pharma, said the company delivered another quarter of strong growth, supported by improved execution across its businesses. He highlighted the 31% growth in the CDMO segment, driven by expanding customer engagements, strategic partnerships and a strong opportunity pipeline.He also noted that continued investments in manufacturing capabilities, innovation and capacity expansion would help the company capitalise on increasing global outsourcing opportunities and create long-term shareholder value.Gland Pharma share price Gland Pharma shares have gained approximately 30% over the past three months. The stock currently commands a market capitalisation of around Rs 51,928 crore.On the technical front, according to Trendlyne data, the stock is trading above seven of its eight simple moving averages (SMAs), indicating strength across most of its tracked moving-average indicators.Disclaimer: The views/recommendations mentioned in this article, wherever applicable, are those of the respective SEBI-registered Research Analyst/brokerage and have been reproduced/reported with due attribution.
